solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Bird call I missed crossing middle of path

indicators.note: the two central letters of path go across, i.e. either side of, the shortened call
the central pair of letters of the word path is taken
the letter I is left out of the call, so it goes missing

parts.note: a voice is a call or cry, as in voicing an opinion

explanation.surface: A birdwatcher fails to hear a call while walking across a footpath.
explanation.walkthrough: 'call' is a noun for a cry, not a phone call; the middle of a four-letter word is its central pair.
explanation.definitionFit: The avocet is a wading bird with an upcurved bill, the emblem of the RSPB.

clue.text: Unclear what comes ashore in Nice?

definitions.meaning: the French word for a sea wave, which a visitor to the Riviera resort would see breaking on the beach

explanation.surface: Someone is puzzled about what washes up on the beach at Nice.
explanation.walkthrough: Nice is the French resort, not the adjective; in French the word for a wave is the same as the English word for unclear.
explanation.definitionFit: Unclear and hazy are synonyms; the second sense is the French noun for a wave, which breaks on the shore.

clue.text: Put an end to lease that's given to painter

parts.note: in American slang to can something is to stop it or fire someone
a let is a lease granted to a tenant, so this phrase is a let
taken as written

explanation.surface: A landlord decides to terminate a lease that was granted to an artist.
explanation.walkthrough: CAN, A LET and TO run together; the painter is the Venetian view-painter of the eighteenth century.
explanation.definitionFit: Canaletto was the Venetian artist famous for detailed views of Venice and London.

clue.text: French city fashion involves person going topless

indicators.note: the fashion word wraps round, i.e. involves, the shortened person

parts.note: ton means fashion or the fashionable world, as in bon ton

indicators.note: the first letter of the person word is removed, as if its top were off

parts.note: a soul is a person, as in not a soul about

explanation.surface: A French city's fashion scene includes someone going topless, perhaps on its beaches.
explanation.walkthrough: Ton (as in bon ton) is an old word for high fashion.
explanation.definitionFit: Toulon is a French port and naval base on the Mediterranean coast of Provence.

clue.text: Speed in rhythmic monologue, one song losing central part

parts.note: rap is rhythmic spoken verse over a beat
the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: the middle letter of the song word drops out

parts.note: a ditty is a short simple song

explanation.surface: A rapper speeds through a monologue and a song that has its middle section cut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing central part' removes the middle T of DITTY, leaving DITY.
explanation.definitionFit: Rapidity is swiftness, the noun from rapid, so a straight synonym for speed.

clue.text: Any tic-tac erring when failing … to indicate this?

definitions.text: Any tic-tac erring when failing … to indicate this?

indicators.note: the letters of the first three words fail, i.e. collapse and are rebuilt in a new order

explanation.surface: A bookie's signaller who gets his hand signals wrong fails to tip a sure winner.
explanation.walkthrough: Tic-tac is the hand-signalling system British racecourse bookmakers use to relay odds; a signaller failing to show a horse as a near-certain winner would be erring badly.
explanation.definitionFit: A racing certainty is a horse, or anything, thought sure to win, the bet a bookie would want flagged.

clue.text: Labourer's request, note, about live current

definitions.note: an adjective: belonging to a common worker

indicators.note: the request and note go about, i.e. round, the next pieces

parts.note: a plea is an earnest request
to be is to exist or live
I is the symbol for electric current in physics

explanation.surface: A worker makes a request about a note concerning live electrical current.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is possessive, so it stands for an adjective: of or like a common worker.
explanation.definitionFit: Plebeian describes the common people of ancient Rome and, by extension, the working classes, so it fits a worker's lot.

clue.text: Democrat sites collectively hacked into by European geek

parts.note: D stands for Democrat in US politics

indicators.note: the European letter breaks into the middle of the web word

parts.note: the web is all websites taken together

explanation.surface: A political party's websites are hacked by a European computer nerd.
explanation.definitionFit: A dweeb is a socially awkward, studious person, American slang close to nerd.

clue.text: Wild figure observed in final uphill crossing

indicators.note: the wild figure is seen inside the reversed word
in a down entry the word for final is read from bottom to top

parts.note: last means final
a raver is a wild partygoer

explanation.surface: A wild man is spotted on the final uphill stretch of a trek.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uphill' works only because this is a down entry, read from the bottom.
explanation.definitionFit: A traversal is the act of going across something, a crossing of a mountain face or region.

clue.text: I'll advise Lance (young crackpot)

indicators.note: crazy, so the letters of the two words go mad and are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone offers to give advice to Lance, who is young and a bit unhinged.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is spoken by the answer itself: a newspaper problem-page writer promising advice.
explanation.definitionFit: An agony uncle is a male advice columnist who answers readers' personal problems.

clue.text: Test moved to the afternoon?

definitions.meaning: read as ex-a.m., no longer in the morning, i.e. formerly a.m.

explanation.walkthrough: Ex means former and a.m. means morning, so something shifted to the afternoon is ex-a.m.
explanation.definitionFit: The short form of examination, a test of a student's knowledge.

clue.text: Ancient water source currently ebbing after interruption by river

parts.note: a well is a source of water

indicators.note: the reversed word is broken into by the river letter
ebbing flows back, so the word for currently runs backwards

parts.note: now means currently

explanation.surface: An old well's flow ebbs after a river cuts across it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ebbing' turns NOW into WON, and R interrupts it to give WORN.
explanation.definitionFit: Well-worn means old and much used, so it stretches to aged and ancient things.

clue.text: Rally not accepting silly mark or symbol

indicators.note: the rally word refuses the silly word, which is taken out

parts.note: to rally troops is to assemble them
an ass is a silly person
M is short for mark, the old German currency

explanation.surface: A rally refuses to tolerate a silly badge or symbol.
explanation.walkthrough: Mark is the former German currency, abbreviated M.
explanation.definitionFit: An emblem is a symbolic badge or device, such as a national flower.

clue.text: American police team positioned to apprehend women

indicators.note: the positioned word catches the women letter inside it

parts.note: sat means placed or positioned

explanation.surface: An American police team is positioned to arrest some women.
explanation.definitionFit: SWAT, Special Weapons and Tactics, is a US police unit for dangerous armed incidents.

clue.text: Wife rubbished his claim, showing capricious mood

indicators.note: his claim is rubbished, i.e. trashed and reassembled in another order

explanation.surface: A wife dismisses her husband's claim, showing a fickle mood.
explanation.definitionFit: Whimsical means fanciful and given to sudden changes of mind, so capricious in mood.

clue.text: Firm with a desire to contain dead fuel waste

parts.note: CO is short for company, a firm

indicators.note: the desire word holds the dead letter inside

parts.note: lust is strong desire

explanation.surface: A company desperate to keep a dead fuel's waste contained.
explanation.definitionFit: Coal dust is the fine powder left over from coal, the waste of that fuel.

clue.text: Perform poem about old lake fish

parts.note: to do a play or act is to perform it

indicators.note: the poem goes about, i.e. round, the next two letters

parts.note: verse is poetry, a poem

explanation.surface: Someone recites a poem about an old lake full of fish.
explanation.walkthrough: O and L sit inside VERSE before its final E.
explanation.definitionFit: Dover sole is a flatfish prized in cooking, named after the Kent port.

clue.text: Uproar and disapproving comment with friend taking husband inside

indicators.note: the friend and husband letters go inside the jeer

parts.note: boo is a jeer of disapproval
an ally is a friend or supporter

explanation.surface: A heckler and a friend bring a husband into a noisy row.
explanation.definitionFit: Ballyhoo is noisy fuss and commotion, near-synonym of uproar and hullabaloo.

clue.text: 50 per cent ruminant changed to 75 per cent of ruminant

indicators.note: the letters of to plus the shortened word are changed into a new order
the eight-letter word keeps its first six letters, three quarters of it

explanation.surface: An odd biology puzzle about a half-animal turning into three quarters of one.
explanation.walkthrough: '75 per cent of' keeps RUMINA from RUMINANT; 'changed' rearranges TO + RUMINA.
explanation.definitionFit: The Minotaur of Greek myth was half man, half bull, and a bull chews the cud.

clue.text: Very ordinary officer showing some potential

parts.note: O is short for ordinary, as in O level
Lt is short for lieutenant, an officer

explanation.surface: A rather ordinary officer shows some promise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'potential' is electrical potential difference, not promise.
explanation.definitionFit: The volt is the unit of electrical potential difference, so a measure of some potential.

clue.text: Odd bits of Urdu on edges of map identifying hills

indicators.note: those letters sit at either edge of the map word
the first and third letters of Urdu, its odd-numbered ones

parts.note: a plan is a map or chart

explanation.surface: Odd fragments of Urdu written at the edges of a map mark out hills.
explanation.definitionFit: Upland is higher hilly ground, a collective term for the hills of a region.

clue.text: Go for a second sea trip

parts.note: a sail is a trip on the sea

explanation.surface: Someone decides to take a second sailing trip.
explanation.definitionFit: To assail is to attack, and to go for someone is the idiom for attacking them.

clue.text: What makes ale singular?

parts.note: split two, two, one, the pieces describe a pair of letters set upon a final E, which in a down entry builds the word ale

explanation.surface: A drinker wonders what makes one ale unique.
explanation.walkthrough: This is a reverse clue: split the answer 2,2,1 and, in a down entry, AL sits on top of E, which spells ale.
explanation.definitionFit: Singular and solitary both mean single, by itself, without company.

clue.text: Harsh mood, according to financial centre dumping leader

parts.note: as per means according to

indicators.note: the first letter of the financial word is dumped

parts.note: the City is London's financial district

explanation.surface: Someone describes a harsh mood in the City after the boss is fired.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dumping leader' drops C from CITY, leaving ITY.
explanation.definitionFit: Asperity is harshness or sharpness of tone or temper, so a harsh mood.

clue.text: Drift anchor one tugged up, though only partly

indicators.note: in a down entry the run of letters is read upwards
only part of the three words anchor one tugged is used

explanation.surface: A drift anchor is hauled up, though only part of the way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drift' is the general meaning or gist, not a boat moving. 'only partly' picks RONET from 'anchor one tugged', and 'up' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: The tenor of a speech is its general drift or gist.

clue.text: Vocal effect occupying the chorus

indicators.note: the run of letters occupies a place inside the two words

explanation.surface: A choral effect fills the chorus.
explanation.definitionFit: An echo is a repeated sound effect, used in singing as a vocal device.

clue.text: Keep close to airport building — certain to see first taking off

parts.note: a hangar houses aircraft at an airfield

indicators.note: the first letter of the certain word departs, like a plane taking off

parts.note: bound means certain, as in bound to see it

explanation.surface: Plane-spotters stay near an airport hangar, sure to see the first plane take off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first taking off' removes B from BOUND, leaving OUND.
explanation.definitionFit: To hang around is to loiter or linger nearby, so to stay close.

clue.text: A parrot biting limb invites symbolic interpretation

indicators.note: the parrot holds the limb in its beak, i.e. contains it

parts.note: a lory is a brightly coloured Australasian parrot
a leg is a limb

explanation.surface: A parrot nipping someone's leg seems to carry a symbolic meaning.
explanation.walkthrough: The lory is a less familiar parrot of Australasia, a crossword regular.
explanation.definitionFit: An allegory is a story whose characters and events carry a hidden symbolic meaning.

clue.text: Sombre doctor, before appointment, dispensing repeated quantity of pills?

indicators.note: the letter that appears twice in the word pills is dispensed with

parts.note: early means ahead of the arranged time

explanation.surface: A gloomy doctor arrives early and hands out repeat prescriptions.
explanation.walkthrough: The repeated element of 'pills' is its doubled L; dispensing it turns EARLY into EARY.
explanation.definitionFit: Dreary means dull and gloomy, close in sense to sombre.
